 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 10.04.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 10.04.2023 at about 03.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EF- 1047 on S.S.Ghati Doddaballapura Road, when he reached near Hadonahalli, Tubagere Hobli, Doddaballapura, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-C-7145 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and thereafter dashed to another car bearing Reg No.KA-06- AB-3947 and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Doddaballapura Government Hospital and later shifted to Sri. Ashwini Hospital, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 34 years and working as Mason and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1- owner has not appeared before the tribunal,
hence, placed exparte.

After service of summons, the respondent No.2- Insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the existence of policy in respect of the car bearing No.KA-41-C-7145.
Further it has denied the involvement of the offending car bearing No.KA-41-C-7145 in the alleged accident.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident by contending that the alleged accident was due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle himself.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further contended that the driver of the offending car did not possessed valid and effective driving licence,
permit and FC at the time of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 10- 04-2023 at about 3-00 p.m, when he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing reg- istration No.KA-50-EF-1047 on S.S. Ghati - Doddaballapura Road near Hadonahalli, Tubagere Hobli,
Doddabal- lapura, Bangalore Rural at that time, the driver of Car bearing registration No.KA- 41-C-7145 drove the same at high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against her.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner fell down and sus- tained grievous injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?

Further examined Sri. Adarsh A.G., the Medical Record officer at Sri Sai Ashwini Hospital, Bengaluru was examined as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P21 to Ex.P24.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.

In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar along with sketch as per Ex.P3 & P.4.
On perusal of Ex.P3 and P.4 the accident spot is in the left portion of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding.

As per the Ex.P3 mahazar the accident is caused within 2 feet from the edge of the left side road in which the petitioner was proceeding (  
 2        ). This shows that the driver of car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 came to extreme right side in a turning and caused the accident.

10. Even though learned counsel for respondent no.2 vehemently argues to consider the contributory negligence due to head on collusion the same cannot be accepted on the basis the contends of Ex.P3 Mahazar.
As discussed above it is very evident that the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 came to his extreme right side as such the contributory negligence cannot be attributed to the petitioner.
11. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of driver of the Car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
The PW.1 was cross-
examined at length by denying the negligence of the driver of car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

Thus, it can be concluded that, the negligence is on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 .
12.
Ex.P9 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
13. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident was caused by the negligent driving by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
14. The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
No rebuttal evidence is placed by either of the respondents.
The charge sheet was came to be filed on the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.

By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the negligence of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10.04.2023 which is caused by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 which is belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was a working as Mason and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 6 months period including 22 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

The petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.
The petitioner initially admitted Ashwini hospital from 10.04.2023 to 25.04.2023 for the period of 16 days.
Thereafter once gain he admitted to Sri Sai Ashwini Hospital from 25.05.2023 to 30.05.2023 for the period of 6 days.
Hence the petitioner spent 22 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner was in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.22,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 22 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The Photographs marked at Ex.P14 shows the present condition of the petitioner and evidence of Doctor establishes the mall union of fracture with Vascular necrosis.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident was caused by the negligent driving by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
14. The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
No rebuttal evidence is placed by either of the respondents.
The charge sheet was came to be filed on the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this Venkatesh Alias Venkateshaiah vs L V Travels on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15294622/
4 regard.
By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the negligence of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145.
15.
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10.04.2023 which is caused by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-41-CT-7145 which is belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 34 years.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident and looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injury sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment,
conveyance.
The petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.
